title: wg: draft-mahy-mls-private-external-02: the root signing key in the GroupContext defeats its own anti-substitution signature
description:
From assay mimid-1wgh.44.14 of /home/mark/PROJECT/IETF/specs/draft-mahy-mls-private-external-02.txt. Posting needs Mark's OK.
1. §3.2 (L237-242) puts root_private_signature_key, a private signing key, in the GroupContext. The GroupContext travels in every GroupInfo, and GroupInfo goes to external joiners and often to the DS (the draft's own external-commit path; MIMI's groupInfo endpoint). Anyone holding a GroupInfo can then sign a forged ExternalEncryptionInfo, which is exactly the DS substitution attack §4.3 says the signature prevents (L533-538). The signing key needs to stay with members (e.g. derived from the epoch secret like the encryption key, with only the public half published).
2. Registries disagree: §5.4 registers external_encryption_info as an MLS Extension Type 0x0011 with Message(s) GI (L665), while §3.2 says ExternalEncryptionInfo is a Safe AAD component, and §5.5.2 registers a component external_encryption_public_key (AD, 0x000B, L694). One structure, two registrations and names.
3. 'SafeSignWithLabel is not used, because there are two different component IDs represented' (L253) is unclear; say which signature construction is used and why.
4. §3.3 (L296): an external sender 'obtains the ExternalEncryptionInfo from the group's most recent commit' but a non-member has no way to get or authenticate commits other than from the DS, which is the party being hidden from; say where it comes from.
5. References: mls-extensions-10 (now -11), mimi-protocol-06, semiprivatemessage-07.
